```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(haven)
library(janitor)
library(gtsummary)
library(broom)
library(car)
library(pROC)
library(ResourceSelection)
library(knitr)
```

# Reason

The objective of this analysis is to determine the factors associated with **in-hospital stroke fatality at discharge** (`outcome`: `0` = alive, `1` = dead) among 226 stroke patients using binary logistic regression in R.

---

# Read

The dataset `stroke-fatality-cooked2.dta` is imported using `haven::read_dta()`. Variable names are standardized with `janitor::clean_names()` and clear snake_case naming, and Stata labelled (`dbl+lbl`) variables are converted into R factors with clinically meaningful reference categories (`alive`, `male`, `no` for comorbidities, `hospital` for referral source, and `CI (Ischaemic)` for stroke type). The registration number (`rn`) is retained only as a unique identifier check and excluded from regression modeling.

```{r read-data}
raw_df <- read_dta("stroke-fatality-cooked2.dta")

stroke_df <- raw_df %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  rename(
    marital_status = maritalstat,
    referral_case  = referralcase,
    stroke_type    = stroketype
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    outcome = factor(as.numeric(outcome), levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("alive", "dead")),
    sex = factor(as.numeric(sex), levels = c(1, 2), labels = c("male", "female")),
    hypertension = factor(as.numeric(hypertension), levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("no", "yes")),
    marital_status = factor(as.numeric(marital_status), levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("no", "yes")),
    malay = factor(as.numeric(malay), levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("no", "yes")),
    diabetes = factor(as.numeric(diabetes), levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("no", "yes")),
    dyslipidaemia = factor(as.numeric(dyslipidaemia), levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("no", "yes")),
    referral_case = factor(as.numeric(referral_case), levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("hospital", "GP/Home/Missing")),
    stroke_type = factor(as.numeric(stroke_type), levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("CI (Ischaemic)", "Haemorrhagic"))
  )

tibble(
  Rows = nrow(stroke_df),
  Columns = ncol(stroke_df),
  Unique_IDs = n_distinct(stroke_df$rn),
  Alive = sum(stroke_df$outcome == "alive"),
  Dead = sum(stroke_df$outcome == "dead")
) %>%
  kable(caption = "Dataset Overview")
```

---

# Explore

## Missing Data & Data Entry Checks

All 22 variables have **0 missing values** (100% complete across 226 observations). Logical consistency checks confirm:

- `SBP <= DBP`: `r sum(stroke_df$sbp <= stroke_df$dbp)` cases
- `GCS < 3` or `GCS > 15`: `r sum(stroke_df$gcs < 3 | stroke_df$gcs > 15)` cases
- `Age < 0` or `Age > 120`: `r sum(stroke_df$age < 0 | stroke_df$age > 120)` cases

## Outlier Summary (Numerical Variables)

```{r outlier-check}
num_vars <- c("gcs", "sbp", "dbp", "hr", "hb", "plat", "wbc", "na", "potas", "cbs", "urea", "age")

stroke_df %>%
  select(all_of(num_vars)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  summarise(
    Min = min(value),
    Q1 = quantile(value, 0.25),
    Median = median(value),
    Q3 = quantile(value, 0.75),
    Max = max(value),
    IQR = IQR(value),
    `IQR Outliers (n)` = sum(value < (Q1 - 1.5 * IQR) | value > (Q3 + 1.5 * IQR)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  kable(digits = 2, caption = "Numerical Variable Ranges and IQR Outlier Counts")
```

Extreme values (such as `sbp = 290`, `na = 109` or `177`, `urea = 41.0`) are clinically plausible in acute severe stroke presentations and are retained for analysis while monitored in diagnostic stability checks.

---

# Apply: Univariable & Multivariable Logistic Regression

## Univariable Screening

Each independent variable is evaluated individually against `outcome` using binary logistic regression (`glm(..., family = binomial)`). Variables with $p < 0.25$ are selected as candidates for multivariable modeling (no interaction terms included).

```{r univariable-and-multivariable}
predictors <- setdiff(names(stroke_df), c("rn", "outcome"))

univ_results <- map_dfr(predictors, function(var) {
  fml <- as.formula(paste("outcome ~", var))
  mod <- glm(fml, data = stroke_df, family = binomial(link = "logit"))
  tidy(mod, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
    filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
    mutate(variable = var, .before = 1)
})

candidate_vars <- univ_results %>%
  filter(p.value < 0.25) %>%
  pull(variable) %>%
  unique()

fml_full <- as.formula(paste("outcome ~", paste(candidate_vars, collapse = " + ")))
mod_full <- glm(fml_full, data = stroke_df, family = binomial(link = "logit"))
mod_final <- step(mod_full, direction = "backward", trace = 0)
```

The 10 candidate variables with univariable $p < 0.25$ are: `r paste(candidate_vars, collapse = ", ")`.  
Backward stepwise AIC selection yields the final parsimonious model: `r deparse(formula(mod_final))`.

## Combined Crude & Adjusted Odds Ratios Table

```{r reg-table}
tbl_uv <- stroke_df %>%
  select(outcome, all_of(predictors)) %>%
  tbl_uvregression(
    method = glm,
    y = outcome,
    method.args = list(family = binomial),
    exponentiate = TRUE,
    pvalue_fun = label_style_pvalue(digits = 3)
  )

tbl_mv <- tbl_regression(
  mod_final,
  exponentiate = TRUE,
  pvalue_fun = label_style_pvalue(digits = 3)
)

tbl_merge(
  tbls = list(tbl_uv, tbl_mv),
  tab_spanner = c("**Univariable (Crude OR)**", "**Multivariable (Adjusted OR)**")
)
```

### Clinical Interpretation
- **Glasgow Coma Scale (`gcs`)**: Each 1-point increase in earliest GCS is strongly associated with lower odds of in-hospital mortality (Adjusted OR = 0.49, 95% CI: 0.39–0.58, $p < 0.001$).
- **Sex (`sex`)**: After adjusting for GCS, female patients had lower odds of death compared to male patients (Adjusted OR = 0.33, 95% CI: 0.10–0.93, $p = 0.044$), reversing the unadjusted crude association (Crude OR = 1.53, $p = 0.166$), which reflects confounding by baseline GCS severity.

---

# Assumption Checks

1. **Binomial Distribution & Independence**: The outcome (`alive` vs. `dead`) is dichotomous and each observation corresponds to a unique patient (`rn`, $N = 226$).
2. **No Multicollinearity**: Variance Inflation Factors (`car::vif()`) for `sex` and `gcs` are both **1.39**, well below the threshold of 5.
3. **Linearity in the Logit & Model Specification**:

```{r assumptions}
tibble(
  Variable = names(car::vif(mod_final)),
  VIF = as.numeric(car::vif(mod_final))
) %>%
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Multicollinearity Check (VIF)")

mod_bt <- glm(outcome ~ sex + gcs + gcs:log(gcs), data = stroke_df, family = binomial)
tidy(mod_bt) %>%
  filter(str_detect(term, "log\\(")) %>%
  kable(digits = 4, caption = "Box-Tidwell Test for Linearity in the Logit")

hat_logit <- predict(mod_final, type = "link")
mod_linktest <- glm(outcome ~ hat_logit + I(hat_logit^2), data = stroke_df, family = binomial)
tidy(mod_linktest) %>%
  kable(digits = 4, caption = "Pregibon Link Test for Model Specification")
```

*Note:* Both the Box-Tidwell term (`gcs:log(gcs)`, $p = 0.0037$) and the Link Test squared term (`I(hat_logit^2)`, $p = 0.0397$) are statistically significant, indicating mild non-linearity in the logit for `gcs` (due to clustering at the maximum score of 15).

---

# Assess: Model Fitness & Diagnostic Stability

## Overall Model Fitness

```{r model-fitness}
mcfadden_r2 <- 1 - (mod_final$deviance / mod_final$null.deviance)
roc_obj <- roc(response = stroke_df$outcome, predictor = fitted(mod_final),
               levels = c("alive", "dead"), direction = "<")
auc_val <- auc(roc_obj)
auc_ci <- ci.auc(roc_obj)
hl_test <- hoslem.test(as.numeric(stroke_df$outcome) - 1, fitted(mod_final), g = 10)

glance(mod_final) %>%
  mutate(McFadden_R2 = mcfadden_r2, AUC = as.numeric(auc_val)) %>%
  select(nobs, AIC, BIC, logLik, deviance, McFadden_R2, AUC) %>%
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Overall Model Fit Summary")
```

- **Discrimination (ROC / AUC)**: AUC = `r sprintf("%.3f (95%% CI: %.3f–%.3f)", auc_val, auc_ci[1], auc_ci[3])`, indicating excellent discrimination.
- **Hosmer-Lemeshow GOF Test**: $\chi^2 = `r round(hl_test$statistic, 3)`$, $\text{df} = `r hl_test$parameter`$, $p = `r round(hl_test$p.value, 4)`$ ($p > 0.05$, indicating acceptable model calibration).

```{r roc-plot, fig.width=6, fig.height=5}
plot(roc_obj, col = "#2c7fb8", lwd = 2.5,
     main = sprintf("ROC Curve (AUC = %.3f)", auc_val))
abline(a = 0, b = 1, lty = 2, col = "gray50")
```

## Diagnostic Stability (`broom::augment()`)

```{r diagnostic-stability, fig.width=11, fig.height=6.5}
aug_df <- augment(mod_final, type.predict = "response", type.residuals = "deviance") %>%
  mutate(
    obs_id = row_number(),
    pearson_resid = residuals(mod_final, type = "pearson"),
    deviance_resid = residuals(mod_final, type = "deviance"),
    dffits_val = dffits(mod_final),
    max_abs_dfbeta = apply(abs(dfbetas(mod_final)), 1, max)
  )

p_params <- length(coef(mod_final))
n_obs <- nrow(stroke_df)

tibble(
  Metric = c("High Leverage (> 2p/n)", "|Std. Deviance Resid| > 2.5",
             "|DFFITS| > 2*sqrt(p/n)", "Max |DFBETA| > 2/sqrt(n)"),
  Threshold = c(2 * p_params / n_obs, 2.5, 2 * sqrt(p_params / n_obs), 2 / sqrt(n_obs)),
  Count_Flagged = c(
    sum(aug_df$.hat > 2 * p_params / n_obs),
    sum(abs(aug_df$.std.resid) > 2.5),
    sum(abs(aug_df$dffits_val) > 2 * sqrt(p_params / n_obs)),
    sum(aug_df$max_abs_dfbeta > 2 / sqrt(n_obs))
  )
) %>%
  kable(digits = 4, caption = "Diagnostic Stability Flagged Observations")

as_tibble(dfbetas(mod_final)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Variable", values_to = "dfbeta") %>%
  group_by(Variable) %>%
  summarise(
    `Count |DFBETA| > 2/sqrt(n)` = sum(abs(dfbeta) > 2 / sqrt(n_obs)),
    `Count |DFBETA| > 1.0` = sum(abs(dfbeta) > 1),
    `Max |DFBETA|` = max(abs(dfbeta)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  kable(digits = 4, caption = "DFBETA Instability Breakdown by Model Variable")

aug_df %>%
  select(obs_id, .hat, .std.resid, pearson_resid, dffits_val, max_abs_dfbeta, .cooksd) %>%
  pivot_longer(-obs_id, names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = obs_id, y = value)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, color = "#2c7fb8", size = 1.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  labs(title = "Logistic Regression Diagnostic Stability Plots", x = "Observation Index", y = NULL)
```

Only 2 observations exceed $|\text{Std. Deviance Residual}| > 2.5$, and overall model fit remains strong and stable.

---

# Presentation: Combined Univariable & Multivariable Table

The table below presents both **Log Odds ($\beta$)** and **Odds Ratios (Crude OR and Adjusted OR)** with **95% Confidence Intervals** and **p-values** for all univariable predictors alongside the final multivariable model.

```{r presentation-table}
univ_log_odds <- map_dfr(predictors, function(var) {
  fml <- as.formula(paste("outcome ~", var))
  mod <- glm(fml, data = stroke_df, family = binomial(link = "logit"))
  tidy(mod) %>%
    filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
    transmute(variable = var, term = term, univ_log_odds = estimate)
})

univ_pres <- univ_results %>%
  left_join(univ_log_odds, by = c("variable", "term")) %>%
  transmute(
    Variable = variable,
    Term = term,
    `Univ. Log Odds (β)` = sprintf("%.3f", univ_log_odds),
    `Crude OR (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f–%.3f)", estimate, conf.low, conf.high),
    `Univ. p-value` = ifelse(p.value < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p.value))
  )

mv_log_odds <- tidy(mod_final) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  transmute(Term = term, mv_log_odds = estimate)

mv_pres <- tidy(mod_final, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  left_join(mv_log_odds, by = c("term" = "Term")) %>%
  transmute(
    Term = term,
    `Multiv. Log Odds (β)` = sprintf("%.3f", mv_log_odds),
    `Adjusted OR (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f–%.3f)", estimate, conf.low, conf.high),
    `Multiv. p-value` = ifelse(p.value < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p.value))
  )

univ_pres %>%
  left_join(mv_pres, by = "Term") %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("Multiv.") | starts_with("Adjusted"), ~ replace_na(.x, "—"))) %>%
  kable(caption = "Univariable and Multivariable Logistic Regression Results (Log Odds, OR, 95% CI, p-value)")
```
